result: The bug was a single off-by-one in `PostController.index`: it passed `page + 1` to `Post.paginate()`, so the validated (1-based, default 1) `page` query value was shifted one page forward — `/posts` and `?page=1` both rendered the second page of results, the last page's worth of posts was unreachable, and the `meta`/`links` the pager renders from described a page one higher than the one requested. I changed `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:16` to pass `page` through unchanged, leaving the ordering (`id desc`), page size (10), and search untouched; in `resources/js/pages/posts/Index.tsx` the pager now uses the `active` flag the paginator already emits to highlight (and mark `aria-current`) the page actually being shown. Added `tests/PostsIndexPagination.test.ts`, which seeds 25 posts against a reset test database and asserts through the real Inertia props that page 1 starts at the newest post, `?page=1` matches the bare `/posts`, pages 1–3 cover all 25 posts exactly once with correct `currentPage`/`from`/`to`/`lastPage` meta, and page 3 is the partial one. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (6 pass, 0 fail) both pass, and `bunx guren check` reports no failures.
